description: A million particles moved by the GPU: helder.scene.render.GpuParticles writes each particle once, when it is born (where, how fast, its colour, sizes and life), and its vertex shader moves it from then on, so a frame's CPU work is only the few thousand born in it and their upload; one instanced draw of a million quads.

The galaxy is a lawn sprinkler's: three arms flung out of the core along directions that turn, slowing as they go, so each arm is a spiral of particles born at different moments; a disc of reddish dust and a bright core. Drag to turn around it, scroll to zoom, tap the disc for a supernova of 20,000 streaks. On a GPU too slow for a million (a software one) it keeps fewer alive, and says so.
